We need to write a JUnit 4 test file NodeTest.java that comprehensively tests all methods in Node. However Node is abstract; we need a concrete subclass for testing. Could use a simple subclass that implements abstract methods minimally, e.g., TestNode extends Node with fields for attributes, children, baseUri, etc. Could use existing classes like Element, TextNode, Document from jsoup but that would require dependencies? In test we assume jsoup library is on classpath; Node belongs to org.jsoup.nodes. So we can use Element and Document from jsoup to test many methods. But to test Node directly, we need a concrete subclass; we can create an inner class in test file that extends Node. Simplify: create MinimalNode extends Node with: - String name - Attributes attributes = new Attributes(); - List childNodes = new ArrayList<>(); - String baseUri = ""; Implement abstract methods: nodeName() returns name; hasAttributes() returns !attributes.isEmpty()? Actually just return true always. attributes() returns attributes; baseUri() returns baseUri; doSetBaseUri(String baseUri) { this.baseUri = baseUri; } ensureChildNodes() returns childNodes; childNodeSize() returns childNodes.size(); outerHtmlHead and outerHtmlTail can just append something simple for testing; maybe just append nodeName and attributes. But many functions rely on traversal, replaceChild, etc., which use ensureChildNodes etc., and siblingIndex. Need to ensure siblingIndex handling works. Simplify: we can just test methods that operate on attributes, parent/children relationships, sibling navigation, wrapping, before/after, etc. For wrap we need parsing HTML via Parser.parseFragment which expects jsoup library; we could rely on that. But we could also test only attribute methods, parent/child management, sibling nodes, traversal, clone, shallowClone, equals, hasSameValue, etc., using our MinimalNode. Wrap uses Parser.parseFragment requiring context element; may be more complex. Could skip testing wrap. Focus on: - attr getter/setter, hasAttr, removeAttr, clearAttributes - baseUri handling: setBaseUri updates node and children - childNode retrieval, childNodes list, childNodesCopy - sibling navigation: siblingNodes, nextSibling, previousSibling - before/after with HTML insertion: we could test adding sibling HTML using Parser; but we need parent node; we can use MinimalNode with a parent that is also MinimalNode. - before(Node) and after(Node) insertion. - unwrap: test moving children up. - replaceWith - remove - clone and shallowClone produce equal outerHtml but not same instance. - equals identity test. - hasSameValue. - html(appendable) returns Appendable. - toString returns outerHtml. - indent maybe not needed. - ownerDocument and root: using Document subclass. But Document class is part of jsoup; we can use Document to test root/ownerDocument. Simplify: use Element and Document from jsoup for many tests; they already implement Node. That ensures integration with parser. Therefore test using real library: create Document doc = Jsoup.parse("

Hello

"); Retrieve elements. Test attr, hasAttr, removeAttr, clearAttributes. Test baseUri: doc.baseUri() default empty; setBaseUri on child element; ensure child's baseUri changes. Test childNode, childNodes, childNodesCopy. Test sibling navigation: siblingNodes, nextSibling, previousSibling. Test before/after with HTML string. Test before(Node) and after(Node) using new Element. Test unwrap: create element with child and unwrap. Test replaceWith: replace element with new. Test remove: ensure parent no longer contains. Test clone vs shallowClone: clone deep copy; modify clone and verify original unchanged. Test equals identity. Test hasSameValue on two elements with same HTML. Test html(appendable) returns same. Test toString. Given complexity, we can write tests accordingly. Need to import org.jsoup.Jsoup, org.jsoup.nodes.* etc. Write JUnit 4 @Test methods. Also need to ensure tests are deterministic. Now produce file NodeTest.java with start marker ###Test START## and end marker ###Test END##. Let's craft code.
